name: Flickr Pro
tagline: Host a personal photo gallery and metadata archive on user-owned storage

pricing.notes: Annual Pro plan divided by 12; exact list price can change.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Up to 1,000 photos/videos total; up to 50 non-public items; Safe-rated and non-commercial content only.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Unlimited full-resolution storage with no monthly upload cap; ad-free browsing, detailed stats and premium support.
tiers.notes: Annual total is $82; a 2-year plan is $148 ($6.17/month equivalent). US prices exclude applicable tax; international USD pricing is higher.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 1,000 items total and 50 non-public photos/videos; only Safe-rated, non-commercial content is allowed
pricing.hiddenCosts: US tax may be added; users outside supported local currencies can be charged the higher tax-inclusive international USD rates ($13 monthly, $96 annual or $170 for 2 years); app-store prices can differ.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Flickr Pro, host a personal photo gallery and metadata archive on user-owned storage. The hard boundary is large photography community, discovery, hosting, moderation, and mobile apps, plus image pipeline quality, models, and workflow polish.
coreLoopDIY: Catalog local photos into a personal gallery and metadata archive on user-owned storage, generate previews, apply non-destructive adjustments, and export selected originals or rendered copies.
whatYouLose: large photography community, discovery, hosting, moderation, and mobile apps
moatNotes: image pipeline quality, models, and workflow polish
ongoingBurden: raw codecs, color management, metadata, previews, face models, GPU support, storage, backups, sync, and export fidelity
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Flickr Pro because photographers pay because image quality, catalog safety, and fast handling of huge libraries matter more than cloning sliders. The recurring cost buys raw codecs, color management, metadata, previews, face models, GPU support, storage, backups, sync, and export fidelity, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Immich
priorArt.desc: Active open-source self-hosted photo and video management platform.

alternatives.name: Immich
alternatives.desc: A superb personal photo archive with mobile backup, metadata, albums, search, maps, and sharing on storage you control; public portfolio polish is modest.

facts.install: Official Docker Compose stack with the server, machine-learning service, Redis, and PostgreSQL
facts.engines: Local ONNX-based CLIP or SigLIP-compatible smart-search models and InsightFace buffalo or antelope face models, with optional CPU or GPU acceleration
facts.dataFormat: Originals and generated library, upload, thumbnail, profile, video, and backup files live under the configured upload location; users, albums, metadata, and embeddings live in PostgreSQL, and ML models are cached locally
facts.gapVsPaid: It is a superb private archive but does not reproduce Flickr's public social graph, groups, discovery, comments, licensing marketplace or portfolio audience.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker Compose, roughly 6–8 GB RAM, local PostgreSQL storage rather than a network share, persistent media and database paths, and TLS or a reverse proxy for remote access

alternatives.name: LibrePhotos
alternatives.desc: Self-hosted photos and video with faces, objects, semantic search, albums, and public links; deployment is a small server, not a button.

facts.install: Clone the monorepo, copy and edit deploy/compose/.env, then start the Docker Compose stack
facts.engines: InsightFace and ArcFace via ONNX Runtime, with buffalo_sc as the default face model; local object, scene, and semantic-search models, optional BLIP captioning, and an optional GPU image
facts.dataFormat: It scans a user-selected photo directory in place; PostgreSQL stores users, indexes, albums, and ML metadata, while thumbnails, protected media, and downloaded models live in configured application volumes
facts.gapVsPaid: It provides private search and sharing, not Flickr's public community, groups, following, discovery, comments and licensing-oriented exposure.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker Compose, an absolute scan-directory mapping, about 4 GB RAM minimum (8 GB recommended for ML), and roughly 10 GB extra disk beyond the photo library

alternatives.name: Lychee
alternatives.desc: A clean self-hosted album gallery with metadata, passworded sharing, downloads, and a simple Docker setup; much less discovery machinery.

facts.install: Docker Compose with the Lychee image and MariaDB; prebuilt and source installs also exist
facts.dataFormat: Uploaded originals and derivatives live in persistent uploads storage; albums, users, metadata and settings live in MariaDB (or another configured database), with separate logs and temporary-data volumes
facts.gapVsPaid: It publishes albums but offers far less automatic search and no Flickr social network, groups, discovery feed, comments community or built-in audience.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker Compose, writable persistent volumes, a database, an APP_KEY, and domain/TLS setup for remote sharing

alternatives.name: PhotoPrism
alternatives.desc: A searchable self-hosted photo library with RAW support, labels, faces, maps, albums, metadata, and share links; library first, social network never.

facts.install: Docker Compose with MariaDB recommended, or SQLite for a smaller installation
facts.engines: TensorFlow FaceNet for face recognition and TensorFlow Nasnet for built-in labels; optional PhotoPrism Vision API, Ollama, OpenAI, or compatible vision backends
facts.dataFormat: Originals remain in the mounted originals folder; sidecars, previews, thumbnails, face embeddings, model assets, and backups live in the storage folder, while indexes, users, albums, and settings live in SQLite or MariaDB
facts.gapVsPaid: It is a searchable private library rather than a public photo community, so Flickr's groups, follows, discovery, comments and licensing exposure disappear.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker Compose, persistent originals, storage, and database mounts with correct permissions, several GB of RAM or swap, and a CPU- and storage-heavy first index

alternatives.name: Photoview
alternatives.desc: Maps existing folders directly into a clean web gallery with RAW, EXIF, users, albums, links, and downloads; your directory tree stays the boss.

facts.install: Docker Compose with SQLite, MariaDB, or PostgreSQL and one or more mounted media folders
facts.engines: Built-in dlib/go-face face detection and recognition; FFmpeg for video processing; optional Mapbox token for maps
facts.dataFormat: Original photos remain in the mounted folder tree; the database stores users, albums, indexes, and face metadata, while a media-cache directory stores thumbnails and optimized video
facts.gapVsPaid: It mirrors your folder tree into a clean gallery but lacks Flickr's social network, public discovery, communities, comments and portfolio audience.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker plus careful volume paths and host-file permissions; safe remote access also needs a reverse proxy or VPN and TLS

alternatives.name: Piwigo
alternatives.desc: The old, dependable gallery engine: private albums, users, metadata, themes, plugins, and mobile upload, paid for in maintenance rather than money.

facts.install: Upload the NetInstall script or release to PHP web hosting, then complete browser setup against MySQL or MariaDB
facts.dataFormat: Originals live under the upload or galleries directories, generated derivatives and configuration stay in the Piwigo tree, and albums, users, metadata, and plugin state live in MySQL or MariaDB
facts.gapVsPaid: It can host a public gallery, but the audience, groups, following, discovery and community interaction that distinguish Flickr are entirely absent.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires PHP web hosting, a database, writable directories, and ongoing web-server, TLS, and plugin maintenance

rejectedAlternatives.name: Flickr Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The free account caps the library at 1,000 items, allows only 50 non-public items, and forbids commercial use; that is not a Pro archive.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Pro plan and a personal local photo catalog DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Flickr Pro in an empty repository.
Use Tauri 2, React, TypeScript, Rust image libraries, SQLite, and local filesystem access; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: catalog local photos into a personal gallery and metadata archive on user-owned storage, generate previews, apply non-destructive adjustments, and export selected originals or rendered copies.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Index selected folders without moving or rewriting originals and store only catalog data in SQLite.
Generate thumbnails and previews, read EXIF, detect duplicates by hash, and monitor file changes.
Provide timeline, folders, albums, ratings, flags, tags, search, and side-by-side compare.
Store edits as reversible parameters for crop, rotate, exposure, contrast, white balance, and saturation.
Render exports to a new folder with explicit color space, quality, size, and metadata choices.
Add catalog backup, missing-file repair, integrity scan, and a clear original-safety guarantee.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out a proprietary raw-rendering engine.
Deliberately leave out hosted cross-device photo sync and client galleries.
Deliberately leave out frontier culling, retouching, and generative models.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
